$about: The one source of the AhaSlides verbal brand rules: what we believe, who we serve, what we say, how we sound and how we write. generate.mjs renders the human page (foundations/brand-voice-rules.html) and the agent feeds (voice-rules.md, voice-rules.agent.json) from this file. Edit a rule here and nowhere else. Text markup is the same as brand/colour-rules.json: **bold**, `code`, ((small print)), [label](href), and a line break is a new line. A rule or section with no environment or kinds takes the one above it. origin names where a rule came from when it was not in brand guidelines v2.2. The retired-wording table is also enforced by lib/screen-lint-copy.js.
title: AhaSlides brand voice rules
lede: The single source for how AhaSlides talks: what we believe, who we serve, what we say and how we write. It follows brand guidelines v2.2 (22 October 2026) and the decisions made since. Visual rules are not here: the design system holds them.

kinds.label: External marketing and sales
kinds.summary: Website, blog, email, social, ads, video, sales material, help centre, partner and press copy. Every rule applies.

kinds.label: Product copy
kinds.summary: Words in the product. The writing rules (sections 10 to 14) plus guidelines/ux-writing.json.

kinds.label: Internal comms
kinds.summary: Slack, documents and updates. The writing rules only (sections 10 to 14).

glance: We take the work out of engagement: more participation, better feedback, less work.
Describe AhaSlides as "an all-in-one engagement platform for teams and classrooms". Never "interactive presentation software".
Lead with what matters to the reader, not with what AhaSlides does. One message at a time.
Playful, Scientific, Above and beyond: clear, human and confident, never childish, corporate or over the top.
British English everywhere, the blog included. Sentence case, no end punctuation on headlines and CTAs, no em or en dash.
One clear, specific call to action per piece, never a hard sell.
AI is an enabler, not the hero. Use "all-in-one", "engagement" and "aha moments" with care.
The brand director (ian@ahaslides.com) owns this file.

rules.text: **Our why.** We believe humans achieve more when they genuinely engage with each other. But getting people involved can be hard work. And we don't think it should be.

**Our how.** We combine playful thinking, scientific curiosity and a genuine care for people to make engagement easier. We use technology, including AI, to take on more of the work, so humans can focus on what matters: connecting, learning and achieving more together.
**Our what.** We're building an all-in-one engagement platform that makes it easier for teams and classrooms to get people participating, learning and sharing what they really think.

blocks.text: What we believe

rules.text: We believe in aha moments: when everyone is tuned in, questions are flying, ideas are bouncing around, and people are laughing, learning and sharing what they really think.

We also believe humans achieve more when they genuinely engage with each other. Creating those moments should be easier: less time preparing, organising, chasing responses and figuring out what it all means, and more time connecting, listening, learning and making things happen together.

blocks.text: There's a buzz you can feel. A sense that something good is happening between people. These are the moments that stick. When something finally clicks. When someone finds their voice. When a team comes together. When people leave knowing, feeling or understanding something they didn't before.
That's why we're building AhaSlides: technology that takes on more of the work around engagement, so people can focus on the moments that matter. More participation. Better feedback. Less work.

rules.text: Our monster is the unnecessary work it takes to get people engaged.

blocks.text: The endless preparation, juggling of tools, chasing of responses and making sense of results that turn getting people involved into another job.
We believe technology should take care of more of that work, so humans can spend less time managing engagement and more time actually engaging.

rules.text: The easiest way to get people involved, gather feedback and make learning stick. All with less work.

rows: Educators and trainers
Learners actively participating and showing what they understand, without creating more work for themselves.
Less work and more participation.
Get more people involved without adding more workload.
Leaders and culture builders
People contributing, sharing what they really think and feeling involved, with a clearer picture of what's happening across the team.
Meaningful feedback and more participation.
Give everyone a way to contribute and get a clearer picture of what your team really thinks.
Event organisers
An energetic, participatory experience that people remember, without complicated tech getting in the way.
Participation and live experiences.
Get the whole room involved, without adding more work behind the scenes.

rules.text: Our positioning stays the same (the easiest way to take the work out of engagement). What we lead with changes according to what matters most to the audience.
For an educator and trainer, less workload and more student participation are equal reasons for them to care.
For leaders and culture builders, "save 20 minutes creating a poll" may be much less exciting than hearing from employees who don't normally speak up.
For an event organiser, it's probably all about the buzz of a live experience.
We help teams and classrooms engage more while working less.

By using AhaSlides, our users spend less time, admin and effort managing engagement; get more people participating; and get more meaningful feedback. If your message communicates at least one of these ideas, you're heading in the right direction.

rules.text: Every external message leans on at least one of the three pillars, and uses its useful language rather than inventing a new angle.

Use these three core opinions to take a side, make a stand and give people a reason to come with us. They are the foundation for what we have to say, and a springboard for more points of view, content ideas and hooks. Instead of simply telling people what AhaSlides does, they say something about the way people work, learn and engage, so people can agree, disagree or side with us.

blocks.text: You can't replace the buzz you feel from a room of fully tuned in people.

When people are genuinely involved, the room takes on a life of its own. Questions change the conversation. Unexpected things happen. People create something together that couldn't have happened without them. You can replay what happened but you can't replay what it felt like.
Getting people involved doesn't have to suck (your time, your energy or your will to carry on).

Hours of prep. More admin. Chasing people for responses. No thank you. Technology should take more of that work off your plate, so you can spend less time making engagement happen and more time actually engaging.
The more AI can do, the more human we need to be.

AI should give us more bandwidth for people, not more ways to avoid them. Sure, it can help us do the work, but we still own the outcome. Care, connection and the conversations that really matter shouldn't be optimised or handed off to robots.

rules.text: Our brand spices are strains of DNA. They can be found in everything we do, and they make us unique and memorable in a busy category. The three are Playful, Scientific, and Above and beyond.

blocks.text: Playful

We're playful people with a playful product. Whether we're designing slides, writing copy, running meetings or launching features, we believe work should spark joy, not just check boxes. Being playful means using humour and creativity to break monotony, lift energy, and bring people together. Because even the most serious professionals are human, and we all engage better when there's a splash of fun.

rules.text: **Playful: how it sounds.** Energetic, witty, and conversational.
**Playful: how we apply it.** Use fun analogies, light humour, and an informal but professional tone. Speak like a friendly expert, not a boring professor. We keep things fun, but never silly.

blocks.text: Scientific

We back everything up with data, insight, and research. Whether we're designing a feature, writing a message, presenting an idea, or supporting a user, we always aim to understand the "why" behind human attention and engagement. Being scientific means grounding our work in evidence, learning from real behaviour, and staying curious about how people think, feel, and connect. It's how we stay credible, useful, and trusted, from the smallest classroom to the largest meeting room.

rules.text: **Scientific: how it sounds.** Clear, insightful, and backed by research.
**Scientific: how we apply it.** Use research and data to reinforce engagement strategies. Avoid vague claims: everything is grounded in evidence. We educate but never lecture.

blocks.text: Above and beyond

We're all about creating "aha moments" for our users and colleagues. Whether it's in our product experience, pricing, communication, customer service, or the way we support each other at work, we aim to work hard to go above the status quo and beyond expectations. Being above means doing better than what's currently out there. And going beyond means doing it with empathy, pride, and real human care. It's about solving problems curiously and delivering more than people hoped for.

rules.text: **Above and beyond: how it sounds.** Confident but humble, thoughtful but not flashy.

**Above and beyond: how we apply it.** Add that extra touch, whether in copy, product interactions, or customer experiences. Make people feel seen, valued, and supported. We deliver aha moments that feel personal and meaningful.

rows: "All-in-one"
Use when describing our platform ambition or breadth. Do not use it as a substitute for explaining the customer benefit.
"Engagement"

This is valuable brand language. Don't overuse it. Save it for moments of human connection, discovery, shared energy or the deeper purpose of AhaSlides.

sections.title: Editorial standard from the brand director

blocks.text: These came from the brand director's reviews of draft copy on 12 and 15 October 2026. They apply to every kind of writing; the social-only rules (post types, LinkedIn, reels) stay with the social writing skill.

rules.text: Clear doesn't mean flat. Once the message is clear, add energy, warmth or personality: clear, conversational, confident writing with a little more life in it.

Judgement, not formula. Not every piece needs a joke, an exclamation mark or a clever hook. If every piece gets a quirk, our copy becomes as predictable as the AI writing habits we are trying to eliminate.
Get to the point. Put the main news, topic, audience problem or benefit near the beginning, and don't bury it beneath an elaborate setup.
Clarity beats cleverness. A clever hook is only useful if it helps communicate the message; don't confuse being creative with being mysterious.

Write like a person, with varied sentence lengths. Don't make every sentence a short, dramatic one-liner, and don't chain subordinate clauses the reader has to untangle. Read a long sentence aloud and simplify it if it sounds awkward.
No artificial suspense, theatrical one-sentence paragraphs or formulaic AI copy, and no detached description of a feature.
Make the audience the hero. Use "you" and "your" where natural, and write from their perspective: what they can achieve, learn or improve.
Respect the reader's time. Remove unnecessary setup, repetition and detail. Concise means removing unnecessary words; clarity matters more than word count.
Bring playfulness into the words themselves: conversational expressions and changes in rhythm, not emojis or exclamation marks alone.
Use punctuation with intention. Exclamation marks add energy when used sparingly: never more than one in a row, and never to make lifeless writing exciting.
Celebrate our news. Launches, achievements and milestones should sound like things we are genuinely pleased about, especially in the opening line, and never like a routine update.
Don't assume the reader has seen earlier messages. Each one must make sense to someone meeting the feature for the first time.
Be direct about what you want people to do: say what to try, why and where. Don't add a generic example to a call to action.
Don't open with "I'm excited to share" and don't write robotic, matter-of-fact announcements.
Don't force humour or personality the author wouldn't naturally use, and avoid a clever line that can be misread.
Don't be overly dry, overly complex (no big words to sound clever) or so corporate, B2B or AI-sounding that it could have come from any software company.

Interrogate your own draft before submitting: is the main point immediately clear, does it sound human, is every sentence earning its place, is the audience benefit obvious, and does the call to action give people a reason to act?
